findings.trigger_condition: Edges contain a hashable node and an unhashable node that evaluate as equal (e.g., frozenset({1}) and set({1})).
findings.root_cause: The _id_of function splits the lookup path based on hashability but fails to cross-check. A hashable value only checks hash_buckets (ignoring previously seen unhashable nodes), and an unhashable value only scans unhashable_nodes (ignoring previously seen hashable nodes).
findings.impact: Equal objects across the hashability boundary are incorrectly assigned different node IDs. This causes the algorithm to treat them as distinct nodes, violating the node deduplication contract. Consequently, it misses dependency cycles (e.g., self-edges represented by an equal hashable/unhashable pair) and outputs duplicate nodes in the layers.
findings.suggested_validation: Test dependency_layers([(frozenset({1}), set({1}))]). It should detect a self-dependency and raise DependencyCycleError, but it incorrectly returns [[{1}], [frozenset({1})]].
